code: retval = addParentAndTypeRef(server, session, node, parentNodeId, referenceTypeId, &item->typeDefinition.nodeId);
note: Attacker-controlled parentNodeId from the decoded AddNodes request (binary MSG chunk) is passed to the parent-reference helper after the new node was already inserted into the nodestore.

code: retval = checkParentReference(server, session, node->nodeClass, parentNodeId, referenceTypeId);
note: The attacker-chosen parent NodeId is forwarded into the parent consistency check.
Lookup of the requested parent fails because the NodeId points to a non-existent node; the function returns UA_STATUSCODE_BADPARENTNODEIDINVALID at line 78.

On the failed parent check, the helper fully deletes the node that is already present in the nodestore: deleteNodeOperation -> removeDeconstructedNode -> UA_Nodestore_remove frees the entry (refCount drops to 0).

Error path unconditionally deletes the node a second time even though addParentAndTypeRef already removed and freed it, so the freed UA_NodeMapEntry is dereferenced again (double free / use-after-free).
UA_Nodestore_delete dispatches to UA_NodeMap_deleteNode, which recomputes the entry from the dangling node pointer and deletes it again.
Members of the already-freed node entry are read (referencesSize, references, browseName, ...) from poisoned/freed memory, producing a read of uninitialized memory (MSan use-of-uninitialized-value).
